sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: Cross-platform path manipulation: Join (concatenate with correct separators), Base, Dir, Ext, Clean, Abs, Rel, Match, WalkDir — the portable path toolkit.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The core functions, executed:

```go
filepath.Join("/usr", "local", "bin")
// "/usr/local/bin" — verified

filepath.Ext("main.go")     // ".go" — verified
filepath.Base("/a/b/c.txt")  // "c.txt" — verified
filepath.Dir("/a/b/c.txt")   // "/a/b"
filepath.Clean("/a/../b//c") // "/b/c"
filepath.Abs("rel/path")     // "/current/dir/rel/path"
filepath.Rel("/a", "/a/b/c") // "b/c" — the relative path between two
filepath.Match("*.go", "main.go") // true — glob matching
```

Why filepath (not path): filepath uses the OS-native separator (/ on Unix, \\ on Windows); the path package is for slash-only URLs. Using filepath means your code works on Windows without changes.

The composition patterns:

Join over string concatenation: "/a" + "/" + "b" works until a component already has a separator — Join handles all cases. It's the ONLY correct way to combine paths.

WalkDir (the modern Walk):
```go
filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
    if d.IsDir() { return nil }
    if filepath.Ext(path) == ".go" { fmt.Println(path) }
    return nil
})
```
— the find-files pattern: walk a tree, filter by Ext, process.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    J[Join usr local bin] --> S[/usr/local/bin]
    E[Ext main.go] → X[.go]
    B[Base /a/b/c.txt] → N[c.txt]
    W[WalkDir root] → CB[each entry callback]
    M[Match *.go] → T[true or false]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The separator abstraction, mechanically: filepath.Join uses the OS's Separator constant (\ on Windows); the implementation normalizes any input separators. The same code produces correct paths on both platforms — the package IS the portability layer.

The Clean semantics: removes redundant separators, resolves . and .. lexically (no filesystem access — purely textual). Clean("/a/./b/../c") = "/a/c". The guarantee: the result is the simplest path naming the same file.

The WalkDir vs Walk evolution: Walk takes an fs.FileInfo (requires stat-ing every file — a syscall each); WalkDir takes fs.DirEntry (the info is already available from the directory read — no extra stat). The Go 1.16+ idiom is WalkDir; the API shape is otherwise identical.

The security check: filepath.Clean on user-provided paths before joining to a root (preventing ../ escape) — the traversal-attack defense. The pattern: clean, then verify the result is still under the root.
